result.situation: Routine non-emergency job: the toilet flush in the second-bedroom WC at Flat 10, 130 Lantern Quay is faulty. The agency asked landlord Ellis whether to send a contractor or let him deal with it himself (event 003). Ellis replied "Yes please mend it" (event 006). Event 005 asked whether the landlord needs a reply.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 006 clearly approves the attendance described in event 003, and classify_reply rated it an unconditional approval (approve=1.0, 0.79, auto). The normal next step is to record the approval and move to provider selection. The landlord didn't name a contractor and none is on record for this property, so I can't assign one without making it up. Property history shows ticket 64 with the same title, description and creation time at this property. That risks two contractors being sent, so the operations team needs to choose a contractor and decide whether the tickets are duplicates.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The approval is clear and nothing needs answering, so a reply wouldn't move the job on.
No contractor is named or on record for this ticket. Picking one would mean inventing a provider, and it could duplicate work on R/PM032-2.
The next step needs an agency decision (which contractor, whether it's a duplicate). Without a queue item the job could stall.
